findings.claim: Asymmetric maintenance coverage: `standing` rows get full row-shape negatives (missing record, missing sha256, unsorted, duplicate id, id outside ^D-[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$, uppercase digest) but `per_job` gets only two — not-a-list and not-sorted. lane-policy.md 'Binding and acceptance' fixes the SAME shape for both lists ('each a list of {"record": <decision id>, "sha256": <show digest>} sorted by unique record id'), so the missing per_job negatives are contract-backed, not invented schema. Surviving mutant: validate applies the full row check to maintenance['standing'] and, for maintenance['per_job'], only `isinstance(rows, list)` plus a sortedness check on [r['record'] for r in rows]. The whole suite stays green while a record binds per_job=[{'record':'job-1','sha256':'F'*64}] — malformed decision id AND uppercase digest admitted. Duplicate per_job record ids are likewise admitted.
findings.reproduce: Add to per_job the five negatives that already exist for standing: missing `record`, missing `sha256`, uppercase digest, duplicate record id, and a record id outside ^D-[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$.

findings.claim: `admission.record` has exactly one pattern negative, 'd-lanes-1', which differs from the valid 'D-LANES-1' only by case. Nothing forces admission.record to be checked against the register pattern lane-policy.md pins at ^D-[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$. Surviving mutant: validate checks admission.record with `isinstance(v, str) and v and v == v.upper()`. It refuses 'd-lanes-1' (test passes) while admitting 'LANES-1', 'XYZ', 'D-LANES-' and 'D_LANES_1'. The standing list DOES carry the structural negative 'LANES-1' (test_standing_decision_id_outside_the_pattern_is_refused), but no test requires the two sites to share a checker, so a two-code-path implementation survives. Also missing: non-string and empty-string admission.record.
findings.reproduce: Add test_admission_record_missing_the_D_prefix_is_refused using 'LANES-1' (mirroring the standing case) plus a non-string admission.record.

findings.claim: `_raises_naming` asserts only `field in str(exc).lower()`, so two of the nine required-field subtests cannot tell which field was named — the very thing Rec6 pins. Subtest field='sha256': 'sha256' is a substring of both 'template_sha256' and 'grants_sha256', so a refusal message naming either satisfies it. Subtest field='path': the record already carries brief.template.path, snapshot.root and harness.isolation.home, and any message mentioning 'path' passes. Surviving mutant: on a policy missing `sha256`, validate raises with the message 'brief.policy.template_sha256 could not be checked' — the subtest is green though `sha256` is never validated as its own field. Refusal behaviour is still forced; only the naming half of Rec6 is unpinned.
findings.reproduce: Assert the qualified token for these subtests, e.g. 'policy.sha256' and 'policy.path', the way the ref subtest already does via `field if field != 'ref' else 'policy.ref'`.

findings.claim: `template_sha256` is pinned only by an inequality negative ('a'*64 vs the fixture's 'c'*64) and the missing-key subtest. It has no case, length or type negative, unlike `sha256` and `grants_sha256`. Surviving mutant: validate compares `policy['template_sha256'].lower() == rec['brief']['template']['sha256'].lower()`, admitting 'C'*64 in the binding against 'c'*64 in the template — contradicting lane-policy.md's 'Digests are 64 lowercase hex characters' and 'template_sha256 must equal the existing brief.template.sha256'. Same family, smaller: `grants_sha256` has uppercase and short negatives but no non-string one, while `sha256` and `ref` both have theirs.
findings.reproduce: Add test_uppercase_template_sha256_is_refused (policy 'C'*64 against template 'c'*64) and test_non_string_grants_sha256_is_refused.

findings.claim: Fixture luck on the positive side of the profile syntax rule. The invalid set is good (empty, uppercase, leading digit, underscore, leading hyphen, slash) but the ONLY valid profile exercised anywhere in the class is 'fixture-only', which contains no digit. lane-policy.md fixes profile ids as [a-z][a-z0-9-]*. Surviving mutant: validate uses `re.fullmatch(r'[a-z][a-z-]*', profile)` — digits forbidden. Every negative still refuses, every positive neighbor still passes, and a legitimate profile id such as 'dev2' or 'lane-policy-v1' is wrongly refused with the suite green.
findings.reproduce: Add a second positive neighbor validating a digit-bearing syntactically valid profile, e.g. 'fixture-only2'.

findings.claim: The one full-binding positive asserts eight fields individually and never asserts the policy survives validate intact. `grants_sha256` and `admission['sha256']` are read back nowhere on the positive path. Surviving mutant: validate normalises or drops brief.policy['grants_sha256'] (e.g. pops it as 'derived, recomputed later') — every red still reds, every neighbor still passes, and the receipt lane-policy.md requires the trusted consumer to compare is silently gone from the record. A single assertEqual(out['brief']['policy'], binding) closes it and costs one line.
findings.reproduce: Replace the field-by-field reads with, or add, `self.assertEqual(out['brief']['policy'], self._binding())`.

findings.claim: Catalogue item 2, empty-set passes, in its latent form. Both subtest loops iterate a collection with no cardinality assertion first: `for field in self._REQUIRED` (9 entries) and `for label, profile in invalid.items()` (6 entries). Neither is reachable-empty today, so this is not a live green-on-nothing, but a later edit that trims `_REQUIRED` — or a merge that drops entries — narrows the check silently and the run still prints the same 'ok' for that method. The class already writes cardinality assertions elsewhere (assertEqual(len(...), 64), assertEqual(len(...), 7)); these two loops are the exception.
findings.reproduce: Prepend self.assertEqual(len(self._REQUIRED), 9) and self.assertEqual(len(invalid), 6) so a shrunken table fails loudly.

findings.where: ops/devlane/dispatch/tests/test_record.py:531 and 616-650 (ref cases) — CONTRACT GAP, reported not invented
findings.claim: The brief asked that a listed structural field not actually fixed by the owning contract be reported rather than schematised. Two such fields, and the author's handling of each: (a) `ref` LENGTH is unspecified. lane-policy.md says only 'full admitted Git id' and 'full lowercase Git id for the repository's object format' — it never fixes 40. The tests nonetheless hard-code 'c'*40 as the valid ref and refuse 'c'*7 as abbreviated. That is defensible for a SHA-1 repository and the author declared it in the record note, but it does pin an unspecified length: it forbids an implementation that requires the 64-char SHA-256 object id, and it equally admits a lax implementation accepting any lowercase hex of length >= 40. (b) brief.policy.`profile` SYNTAX is fixed only transitively: lane-policy.md pins [a-z][a-z0-9-]* for the ids in the policy file's `profiles` mapping, while the 'Binding and acceptance' section names brief.policy.profile without restating a syntax. Treating them as the same alphabet is one inference step, not a quotation. Neither is a reason to block; both should be named in the contract before the implementer treats the tests as the spec.
findings.reproduce: Amend lane-policy.md 'Binding and acceptance' to state the Git object-id length brief.policy.ref must carry, and to restate that brief.policy.profile is a profile id matching [a-z][a-z0-9-]*.
